The quality of this frontmatter directly affects how AI systems understand each Senshac page. Audit that every route served by Senshac passes rich, meaningful meta to the converter. Checklist per route: title is set to the project/page name (not just 'Senshac'), description is a real sentence about the page content (not empty), og:image resolves to a real R2 media URL via media.senshac.com. title: Add RFC 8288 Link response headers to senshac.com for agent discovery
description: isitagentready.com reports: no Link headers found on homepage. RFC 8288 Link response headers let agents discover machine-readable resources (llms.txt, sitemap, api-catalog) directly from HTTP headers without parsing HTML. For Senshac these should point to: llms.txt (rel=describedby), sitemap.xml (rel=sitemap), and the contact API (rel=service-desc or service-doc). Implementation via Cloudflare Transform Rules (no code change) or a Cloudflare Worker wrapping the static Pages response. Example headers to add: Link: </llms.txt>; rel="describedby", Link: </sitemap.xml>; rel="sitemap". Add to homepage (/) and ideally all pages. Cloudflare Transform Rule path: dashboard > Rules > Transform Rules > Modify Response Header > add Link header matching all routes. Validate: POST https://isitagentready.com/api/scan {"url":"https://senshac.com"} and check checks.discoverability.linkHeaders.status = pass. Skill: https://isitagentready.com/.well-known/agent-skills/link-headers/SKILL.md. Docs: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8288, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9727#section-3

title: Publish DNS-AID SVCB records under _agents.senshac.com for DNS-based agent discovery
description: isitagentready.com reports: DNS for AI Discovery (DNS-AID) well-known entrypoint records not found. DNS-AID lets agents discover service endpoints directly via DNS without hitting any HTTP endpoint first. For Senshac this means publishing SVCB/HTTPS records under the _agents subdomain pointing to our Cloudflare Workers endpoints. Minimum viable: publish _index._agents.senshac.com SVCB record pointing to the site. Extended: publish _a2a._agents.senshac.com if/when an A2A agent endpoint is added. Steps: 1) Add SVCB record in Cloudflare DNS for senshac.com zone: _index._agents.senshac.com. 3600 IN SVCB 1 senshac.com. alpn=h2,h3 port=443. 2) Enable DNSSEC on the senshac.com zone in Cloudflare dashboard (DNS > Settings > DNSSEC) — Cloudflare handles key management automatically. 3) Validate via: POST https://isitagentready.com/api/scan {"url":"https://senshac.com"} check checks.discoverability.dnsAid.status = pass. Note: DNSSEC propagation takes up to 48h after enabling. Skill: https://isitagentready.com/.well-known/agent-skills/dns-aid/SKILL.md. Docs: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-mozleywilliams-dnsop-dnsaid/, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9460

title: Declare Content Signals preferences in senshac.com robots.txt
description: isitagentready.com reports: no Content Signals found in robots.txt. Content Signals (IETF draft contentsignals) let site owners declare explicit AI usage preferences in robots.txt so agents and crawlers know whether content can be used for ai-train, search indexing, and ai-input. The current robots.txt (src/pages/robots.txt.ts) already blocks named AI training bots (GPTBot, CCBot, anthropic-ai, etc.) via Disallow but does not use the standard Content-Signal header. Senshac's content is a portfolio of interior design work — the owner should decide the policy. Suggested policy: ai-train=no (portfolio images should not train models), search=yes (searchability is valuable), ai-input=yes (agents helping users find an interior designer is fine). Implementation: add Content-Signal: ai-train=no, search=yes, ai-input=yes to the User-agent: * block in robots.txt.ts. Optionally use Cloudflare AI Crawl Control dashboard to manage this without code. Acceptance: isitagentready.com scan reports checks.botAccessControl.contentSignals.status = pass. Owner decision needed on policy before implementing. Skill: https://isitagentready.com/.well-known/agent-skills/content-signals/SKILL.md. Docs: https://contentsignals.org/, https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-romm-aipref-contentsignals/

title: Design Senshac meta-repo and focused bare-repo workspace split
description: Evaluate and stage a Senshac workspace split that uses a meta-repo plus focused bare repositories to reduce recurring dx/fx/wt/sd/ml/cn/tr friction for humans and agents. Target shape to evaluate: a local or tracked meta-repo that owns orchestration docs, shared AGENTS guidance, secret placement policy, worktree conventions, and cross-repo scripts; focused bare repos for senshac-web, senshac-content, senshac-infra, senshac-runner, and senshac-media-runner where each repository has a narrow Flox environment, Worktrunk config, git-native trackers, and CI surface. Tooling intent: agents should use Terrarium as the routine planning and prioritization surface (for example tr triage and related graph subcommands), while Seeds remains the issue mutation and integrity source of truth. Non-goals: do not move application code before proving the workflow; do not duplicate secrets into worktrees; do not split Tina content or Cloudflare infrastructure until deployment, preview, and local act flows are mapped. Acceptance: document the proposed topology and migration order; decide whether the meta-repo is a real GitHub repo or local-only wrapper; define what stays in NacoSolutions/senshac versus moves to focused repos; map current seeds and blockers to the target repos; prove a small prototype with one focused bare repo and one worktree; document when to use tr triage versus sd direct commands; update AGENTS.md/workflow docs; link or supersede related seeds such as senshac-50a2, senshac-6762, senshac-3da6, and senshac-ab7d; run seed integrity and relevant workflow checks.

title: Implement fx/dx repo-scoped command pass-through
description: Implement and document repo-scoped command execution so agents can replace cd <worktree> && flox activate -d . -- <command> and cd <worktree> && direnv exec . <command> with stable wrapper forms. Intended contract: fx keeps Flox verbs such as install/uninstall/upgrade/list available as fx <flox verb> conveniences, but otherwise fx -d <path> <command> runs the command through flox activate -d <path> -- <command>. dx mirrors this for direnv: dx -d <path> <command> runs direnv exec <path> <command>. Current verified behavior before implementation: fx -d <path> run sd create --help works, but fx -d <path> sd create --help falls through incorrectly, and --run forms are unsupported. Acceptance: implement pass-through without requiring a run subcommand; preserve explicit Flox management verbs; add or update tests for argv preservation, paths with spaces, command-not-found/failure exit codes, and execution from outside the repo wrapper; update usage/help text and AGENTS guidance; verify examples such as fx -d <worktree> sd create --help and dx -d <worktree> tr triage. This supports the workspace split epic senshac-7bd8 and should align with Terrarium-first triage guidance.

title: Install locked dependencies before pre-push verification
description: Pre-push verify:ci can produce false drift when a persistent worktree has stale node_modules. The failed push rewrote Tina schema version metadata from stale installed packages, while a fresh frozen install generated the committed schema. Acceptance: make the pre-push package contract install dependencies with bun install --frozen-lockfile before verify:ci; update workflow contract coverage; verify the pre-push gate from main.

title: Use Flox Tina CLI for deterministic builds

title: Clean install dependencies in pre-push gate

A failed main push used stale knip even after bun install --frozen-lockfile. Acceptance: make check:prepush remove node_modules before the frozen install, update workflow contract/docs, and verify the push gate from main.

title: Containerized CI runner hangs during Astro/Vite build
description: The GHCR Flox runner image successfully starts CI, checkout, and bun install, but bun run verify:ci hangs inside bun run build at Astro/Vite startup. Local reproduction: podman run --rm -v <worktree>:/work:Z -w /work ghcr.io/nacosolutions/senshac-ci-runner:latest sh -lc 'mkdir -p /usr/bin && ln -sf /bin/env /usr/bin/env && CI=1 bun run build'. It reaches Tina build complete, @astrojs/cloudflare setup, Vite warnings, then stalls before content sync. Tested and did not fix: writable HOME/XDG_CACHE_HOME, ASTRO_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1, Vite optimizeDeps noDiscovery/include=[], Cloudflare imageService passthrough, and skipping @tinacms/astro integration. CI was restored to Flox actions until this is resolved. Also verified the image itself lacks /usr/bin/env; scripts/build-ci-runner now adds that compatibility layer.
closeReason: Resolved by adding glibc to the Flox runner closure and exposing its runtime at /lib64 so Cloudflare workerd can execute. Clean-clone container verification now completes bun run verify:ci with exit 0. Also added findutils and fail-loud handling for the repository cleanliness scanner exposed by the container gate.

title: Shrink Pages Function below Cloudflare deployment limit
description: Production deployment of commit 63f8c5e failed because the generated Pages Function was 14.7 MiB/736 modules, above the account 3 MiB Worker limit. Isolate public rendering to Astro content and lightweight tina-field annotations; disable the unused public Tina island endpoint (404) while retaining /admin editing. Separate visual-editing server islands require a dedicated editor deployment/follow-up rather than sharing the public Worker. Before: ~16 MB/737 files; after: 2,734,858 raw bytes/88 files and ~631 KB aggregate gzip. Add a conservative 3,000,000-byte raw CI guard. Acceptance: dx bun run deploy succeeds on the current plan, Wrangler reports an active production deployment for the source commit, canonical WIP serves the new artifact, and full verify:ci passes.
